request: Extend the workspace structural corpus into a multi-resolution architecture map: an authored ~15-node concept layer above the existing file-anchored elements, concept and element edges derived mechanically from four coupling classes (imports, state-file handshakes, project.json config keys, Skill() invocations in prose), per-element PlantUML shards composed via !startsub/!includesub, views generated on demand rather than stored, and three-case staleness (moved/dangling/stale via anchor content digest). Resolves living-system-model vision §3.3 (diagram altitude taxonomy) and §3.5 (index construction).
novelty_evidence: No live spec covers this — docs/specs/ holds only erp-portables, mvp-sprint-parallel-cycles, release-workflow. Roadmap Epic 7 (living-system-model) is CLOSED with all six slices landed (e7f00de..27c18a6), so no open roadmap item covers it. docs/vision/living-system-model.md §3.3 (diagram core vs optional tail) and §3.5 (index construction) are explicitly-unresolved open questions in a note that states it is 'input to /triage, not output of it'. The concept layer, four-class edge derivation, shard storage and digest-based staleness are new surface with no in-repo precedent.
track_reason: Human picked `power` over the `novel`-default `intake-full` (AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-05), confirming the 5-ticket batch in the same exchange. Power is LIGHTER than the leanest-safe default here, not heavier: its DAG starts at /spec, so intake/scout/research are excepted. Residual accepted and recorded for gate A — discovery exists in the originating session transcript (diagram-volume and corpus measurements, PlantUML preprocessor semantics verified via context7 per Art. VI.5, baseline-v2 docs/thought-compiler/memory prior-art review, and the 15-node concept partition validated empirically at 77% intra-concept import locality) but NOT as reviewable docs/scout or docs/research artifacts. The spec SHALL carry that evidence inline so gate A reviews measurements rather than assertions.

tickets.title: Concept layer — the authored abstraction level
tickets.done_record: The 15 authored concept nodes exist with verified membership; every member path resolves on disk or the write is refused; multi-membership is representable (git_commit_guard belongs to both consent-gates and git-policy); concept nodes carry no anchor by construction and the model says so rather than faking one.

tickets.title: Edge derivation — four coupling classes plus roll-up
tickets.done_record: Element-to-element edges derive from imports, state-file path literals, projectGet config keys, and Skill() invocations in prose; each edge carries provenance derived|authored; roll() lifts element edges to concept level; no edge is authored that a scanner could have derived.

tickets.title: Shard storage and on-demand view generation
tickets.done_record: One PlantUML shard per element delimited by !startsub <element-id>; a view is generated by composing matching shards via !includesub and rendering with the local jar; no WorkspaceView file is ever written (epic D3 stands); the remote MCP renderer is not on the composition path because it cannot resolve local includes.
tickets.security_reason: composes shard files into a generated document and shells out to `java -jar` — an untrusted-input composition and command-execution surface

tickets.title: Three-case staleness — moved, dangling, stale
tickets.done_record: Elements carry anchor_digest over the anchored file's exported symbol surface; reconcile classifies moved (anchor still matches, no action), dangling (anchor matches nothing, fail-closed) and stale (anchor resolves, digest moved); a comment-only edit does not demote every diagram.
tickets.security_reason: resolves caller-influenced anchor globs against the filesystem — the path-traversal and ReDoS surface already fixed once in be48ab9 for this subsystem

tickets.title: Retrieval and surfacing — the descent path
tickets.done_record: A design query descends concept to subsystem to element to code; a maintenance query enters at a touched path and walks up; the concept map is injected at session start in place of the stale-count table; the map routes and code witnesses, so no diagram is ever cited as evidence.

tickets.title: Drift checker — AC span expansion and self-evidence exclusion
tickets.done_record: scoreAgainstDiff expands `AC-lo..AC-hi` spans so interior ids resolve, and refuses reversed spans; EXCLUDED_DIFF_PREFIXES gains `.claude/state/` so the checker's own report is never evidence for the ids it just reported unresolved. Plus two hardenings folded in at the human's direction: (1) composeView now calls assertSafeFieldValue('title') , closing the MEDIUM PlantUML directive injection from the 2026-08-05 security review; (2) a control-byte gate over tracked text files, with the two pre-existing NUL sentinels it found removed from index-io.mjs and document-gate.mjs by rewriting the glob expansion as a single-pass replace (equivalence asserted over 16 globs before writing). 8 new tests; suite 2218 green.
tickets.added_mid_cycle: Added after this workflow's own drift-check-tick reported 9 of 23 ACs unresolved, all of which had passing scenarios — the checker could not see through the `(AC-004..AC-008)` range notation in file-header comments. Fixing the checker rather than rewording the comments was the human's call (the alternative would have taught the tooling nothing). The self-evidence defect was found WHILE writing the range tests: a test passed for the wrong reason because it ran the checker twice, and the second run scored ids against the first run's untracked report. NOT part of the architecture-map feature — it is workflow tooling repaired in flight, so it carries no spec anchor and lands as its own commit in the split.
